A.explanation: A pressure of $1 \times 10^0 \text{ Pa}$ would need a contact area of $600 \text{ m}^2$, far larger than two feet.

B.explanation: A pressure of $1 \times 10^2 \text{ Pa}$ would need a contact area of $6 \text{ m}^2$, still much larger than the area of two feet.

C.explanation: With total foot area about $0.05 \text{ m}^2$, $p = 600/0.05 \approx 1.2 \times 10^4 \text{ Pa}$, closest to $1 \times 10^4 \text{ Pa}$.

D.explanation: A pressure of $1 \times 10^6 \text{ Pa}$ would need a tiny area of $0.0006 \text{ m}^2$, like stiletto heels, not two flat feet.

hints: Start from the 600 N weight as the force $F$ in $p = F/A$, where $A$ is the total contact area of both flat feet.
Estimate one foot as about $0.25 \text{ m}$ long by $0.10 \text{ m}$ wide, so two feet give $A$ of order $0.05 \text{ m}^2$ in $\text{m}^2$.
Divide $600 \text{ N}$ by your area estimate and round the result in $\text{Pa}$ to the nearest power of ten to match one of the options.
walkthrough: The force pressing on the ground is the man's weight, $F = 600 \text{ N}$, spread over the contact area of both feet flat on the ground.
Use the definition of pressure: $p = F/A$, with $F$ in $\text{N}$, $A$ in $\text{m}^2$ and $p$ in $\text{Pa}$.
Estimate the area: one foot is roughly $0.25 \text{ m} \times 0.10 \text{ m} = 0.025 \text{ m}^2$, so two feet give $A \approx 0.05 \text{ m}^2$.
Substitute: $p \approx 600/0.05 = 12000 \text{ Pa} \approx 1 \times 10^4 \text{ Pa}$ after rounding to one power of ten.
This is option C, while the other powers of ten would require areas thousands of times too large or too small for human feet.
